    <article class="article-container">
        
        <header class="article-header">
            <span class="article-category">Campaign Launch</span>
            <h1 class="article-title">Peace of Mind<br>in Your Palm</h1>
            <p class="article-subtitle">Showing modern families how connection and protection can feel simple, intuitive, and deeply human.</p>
        </header>

        <div class="hero-visual-container">
            <img src="../../assets/images/01_FSA.png" alt="Family Safety App Launch">
        </div>

        <div class="article-layout">
            
            <!-- LEFT: Metadata -->
            <aside class="article-sidebar-left">
                <div class="meta-block">
                    <span class="meta-label">Timeline</span>
                    <span class="meta-value">2020 Launch</span>
                </div>
                <div class="meta-block">
                    <span class="meta-label">Role</span>
                    <span class="meta-value">Campaign Strategy &<br>Creative Direction</span>
                </div>
                <div class="meta-block">
                    <span class="meta-label">Disciplines</span>
                    <span class="meta-value">Narrative Strategy<br>Hero Film<br>Modular Design</span>
                </div>
            </aside>

            <!-- CENTER: Narrative -->
            <div class="article-content">
                <p class="lead-paragraph">
                    In a year when "together" felt more precious than ever, Microsoft needed to position Family Safety as the go-to tool for modern parents. We needed to show that peace of mind can be simple, intuitive, and deeply human.
                </p>

                <h2>The Challenge</h2>
                <p>
                    The challenge wasn't just launching another app; it was creating a conversation starter rather than a surveillance tool.
                </p>

                <h3>Strategic Approach</h3>
                <p>
                    As Campaign Strategy & Creative Direction lead, I orchestrated cross-functional teams across Microsoft's product, marketing, and creative divisions. Our goal: develop a globally resonant campaign that balanced technological innovation with authentic family dynamics.
                </p>
                
                <p>
                    We built a <strong>Modular Campaign Architecture</strong>: a scalable Bill of Materials spanning digital, social, and in-app touchpoints. This enabled seamless global deployment while maintaining consistent family-first messaging.
                </p>

                <h3>Impact & Results</h3>
                <p>
                    Within weeks of launch, tens of thousands of families adopted the app and shared heartfelt stories of feeling safer and more connected. Social buzz spiked, and tech press praised our human-centric hero film—proof that narrative-driven marketing builds real emotional resonance.
                </p>
                <p>
                    Families told us they traded "Where are you?" texts for a collective exhale. They could rest easy knowing everyone could be reached with a tap. The campaign achieved its guiding light: bringing families together by helping every family feel safe, seen, and supported.
                </p>

                <h3>Key Learnings</h3>
                <p>
                    This campaign reinforced that when launching a tool as personal as family safety, the narrative must lead with empathy and empowerment, not features and functions. By centering authentic family moments, we created a foundation for sustained adoption and genuine emotional connection.
                </p>

                <!-- EDITORIAL NOTE -->
                <div class="editorial-note">
                    <span class="editorial-label">Perspective & Sourcing</span>
                    <p class="editorial-text">
                        This article reflects professional experience and opinion. Sources are included when referencing external research or data; otherwise, it draws from real-world practice rather than universal rules.
                    </p>
                </div>
            </div>

            <!-- RIGHT: Stats -->
            <aside class="article-sidebar-right">
                <div class="statement-card">
                    <span class="stat-number">3x</span>
                    <span class="stat-label">Engagement Rate</span>
                </div>
                <div class="statement-card">
                    <span class="stat-number">100M+</span>
                    <span class="stat-label">Campaign Impressions</span>
                </div>
                <div class="statement-card">
                    <span class="stat-number">85%</span>
                    <span class="stat-label">Sentiment Lift</span>
                </div>
                <div class="quote-card">
                    "Our guiding light never wavered: design and build with the goal of bringing families together."
                </div>
            </aside>

        </div>

    <!-- MOBILE MENU SCRIPT -->
    <script>
        const mobileToggle = document.querySelector('.mobile-toggle');
        const mobileOverlay = document.querySelector('.mobile-menu-overlay');
        const icon = mobileToggle.querySelector('i');

        mobileToggle.addEventListener('click', () => {
            mobileOverlay.classList.toggle('is-open');
            if (mobileOverlay.classList.contains('is-open')) {
                icon.classList.remove('fa-bars');
                icon.classList.add('fa-xmark');
            } else {
                icon.classList.remove('fa-xmark');
                icon.classList.add('fa-bars');
            }
        });
    </script>
